513.flavor: This Pokémon lives in caves in volcanoes. The fire within the tuft on its head can reach 600 degrees Fahrenheit.

514.flavor: When it gets excited, embers rise from its head and tail and it gets hot. For some reason, it loves sweets.

515.flavor: The water stored inside the tuft on its head is full of nutrients. Plants that receive its water grow large.

516.flavor: It prefers places with clean water. When its tuft runs low, it replenishes it by siphoning up water with its tail.

517.flavor: It eats dreams and releases mist. The mist is pink when it’s eating a good dream, and black when it’s eating a nightmare.

518.flavor: It drowses and dreams all the time. It’s best to leave it be if it’s just woken up, as it’s a terrible grump when freshly roused from sleep.

519.flavor: It’s forgetful and not very bright, but many Trainers love it anyway for its friendliness and sincerity.

520.flavor: These bright Pokémon have acute memories. Apparently delivery workers often choose them as their partners.

521.flavor: This Pokémon is intelligent and intensely proud. People will sit up and take notice if you become the Trainer of one.

522.flavor: Its mane shines when it discharges electricity. They use the frequency and rhythm of these flashes to communicate.

523.flavor: They have lightning-like movements. When Zebstrika run at full speed, the sound of thunder reverberates.

524.flavor: When it detects a noise, it starts to move. The energy core inside it makes this Pokémon slightly warm to the touch.

525.flavor: It relies on sound in order to monitor what’s in its vicinity. When angered, it will attack without ever changing the direction it’s facing.

526.flavor: Although its energy blasts can blow away a dump truck, they have a limitation— they can only be fired when the sun is out.

527.flavor: It emits ultrasonic waves as it flutters about, searching for its prey—bug Pokémon.

528.flavor: The auspicious shape of this Pokémon’s nose apparently led some regions to consider Swoobat a symbol of good luck.

529.flavor: It’s a digger, using its claws to burrow through the ground. It causes damage to vegetable crops, so many farmers have little love for it.

530.flavor: Known as the Drill King, this Pokémon can tunnel through the terrain at speeds of over 90 mph.

531.flavor: This Pokémon has a kind heart. By touching with its feelers, Audino can gauge other creatures’ feelings and physical conditions.

532.flavor: Timburr that have started carrying logs that are about three times their size are nearly ready to evolve.

533.flavor: Gurdurr excels at demolition—construction is not its forte. In any case, there’s skill in the way this Pokémon wields its metal beam.

534.flavor: When going all out, this Pokémon throws aside its concrete pillars and leaps at opponents to pummel them with its fists.

535.flavor: It uses sound waves to communicate with others of its kind. People and other Pokémon species can’t hear its cries of warning.

536.flavor: On occasion, their cries are sublimely pleasing to the ear. Palpitoad with larger lumps on their bodies can sing with a wider range of sounds.

537.flavor: This Pokémon is popular among the elderly, who say the vibrations of its lumps are great for massages.

538.flavor: They train in groups of five. Any member that can’t keep up will discard its belt and leave the group.

539.flavor: The karate chops of a Sawk that’s trained itself to the limit can cleave the ocean itself.

540.flavor: Since this Pokémon makes its own clothes out of leaves, it is a popular mascot for fashion designers.

541.flavor: It protects itself from the cold by wrapping up in leaves. It stays on the move, eating leaves in forests.

542.flavor: It keeps its eggs warm with heat from fermenting leaves. It also uses leaves to make warm wrappings for Sewaddle.

543.flavor: Its fangs are highly venomous. If this Pokémon finds prey it thinks it can eat, it leaps for them without any thought of how things might turn out.

544.flavor: Whirlipede protects itself with a sturdy shell and poisonous spikes while it stores up the energy it’ll need for evolution.

545.flavor: Scolipede engage in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch. At the end of one of these battles, the victor makes a meal of the loser.

546.flavor: Weaving together the cotton of both Cottonee and Eldegoss produces exquisite cloth that’s highly prized by many luxury brands.

547.flavor: As long as this Pokémon bathes in sunlight, its cotton keeps growing. If too much cotton fluff builds up, Whimsicott tears it off and scatters it.

548.flavor: The leaves on its head are highly valued for medicinal purposes. Dry the leaves in the sun, boil them, and then drink the bitter decoction for remarkably effective relief from fatigue.

549.flavor: I suspect that its well-developed legs are the result of a life spent on mountains covered in deep snow. The scent it exudes from its flower crown heartens those in proximity.

550.flavor: Though it differs from other Basculin in several respects, including demeanor—this one is gentle—I have categorized it as a regional form given the vast array of shared qualities.

551.flavor: Sandile is small, but its legs and lower body are powerful. Pushing sand aside as it goes, Sandile moves through the desert as if it’s swimming.

552.flavor: Although this Pokémon has specialized eyes that allow it to see in the dark, Krokorok won’t move much at night—the desert gets cold after sunset.

553.flavor: While terribly aggressive, Krookodile also has the patience to stay hidden under sand for days, lying in wait for prey.

554.flavor: This popular symbol of good fortune will never fall over in its sleep, no matter how it’s pushed or pulled.

555.flavor: This Pokémon’s power level rises along with the temperature of its fire, which can reach 2,500 degrees Fahrenheit.

556.flavor: Once each year, this Pokémon scatters its seeds. They’re jam-packed with nutrients, making them a precious food source out in the desert.

557.flavor: It first tries to find a rock to live in, but if there are no suitable rocks to be found, Dwebble may move in to the ports of a Hippowdon.

558.flavor: Its thick claws are its greatest weapons. They’re mighty enough to crack Rhyperior’s carapace.

559.flavor: It protects itself with its durable skin. It’s thought that this Pokémon will evolve once its skin has completely stretched out.

560.flavor: While mostly known for having the temperament of an aggressive ruffian, this Pokémon takes very good care of its family, friends, and territory.

561.flavor: A discovery was made in the desert where Sigilyph fly. The ruins of what may have been an ancient city were found beneath the sands.

562.flavor: The spirit of a person from a bygone age became this Pokémon. It rambles through ruins, searching for someone who knows its face.

563.flavor: There are many depictions of Cofagrigus decorating ancient tombs. They’re symbols of the wealth that kings of bygone eras had.

564.flavor: Tirtouga is considered to be the ancestor of many turtle Pokémon. It was restored to life from a fossil.

565.flavor: This Pokémon emerges from the water in search of prey despite the fact that it moves more slowly on land.

566.flavor: Archen is said to be the ancestor of bird Pokémon. It lived in treetops, eating berries and bug Pokémon.

567.flavor: Though capable of flight, Archeops was apparently better at hunting on the ground.

568.flavor: This Pokémon was born from a bag stuffed with trash. Galarian Weezing relish the fumes belched by Trubbish.

569.flavor: The toxic liquid it launches from its right arm is so virulent that it can kill a weakened creature instantly.

570.flavor: A once-departed soul, returned to life in Hisui. Derives power from resentment, which rises as energy atop its head and takes on the forms of foes. In this way, Zorua vents lingering malice.

571.flavor: With its disheveled white fur, it looks like an embodiment of death. Heedless of its own safety, Zoroark attacks its nemeses with a bitter energy so intense, it lacerates Zoroark's own body.

572.flavor: They pet each other with their tails as a form of greeting. Of the two, the one whose tail is fluffier is a bit more boastful.

573.flavor: A special oil that seeps through their fur helps them avoid attacks. The oil fetches a high price at market.

574.flavor: Even when nobody seems to be around, Gothita can still be heard making a muted cry. Many believe it’s speaking to something only it can see.

575.flavor: On nights when the stars shine, this Pokémon’s psychic power is at its strongest. It’s unknown just what link Gothorita has to the greater universe.

576.flavor: A criminal who was shown his fate by a Gothitelle went missing that same day and was never seen again.
